title: In India’s capital, Delhiites reduced to documents
content: Across SIR hearing centres in the national capital, people are making repeated trips, producing documents, and waiting for hours to prove their eligibility, often despite having voted for years. Ishita Mishra and Suruchi Kumari spoke to people appealing to retain their right to vote and officials who share the reality of a process marked by confusion. As always, the burden to prove their identity is falling hardest on society’s poorer, less-documented voter

title: Karnataka ranks third in NITI Aayog’s electric mobility index 2025
content: Delhi topped the overall rankings with a score of 84, followed by Maharashtra with 78. Karnataka secured 73

title: Study attempts to find out how India made expensive diabetes medicines affordable
content: India’s low medication prices are tied to its role as a major pharmaceutical exporter, supported by legislation that prevents ‘patent evergreening’ and enables generic drug manufacturing, says a study by diabetologists

title: 'Trump's threats won't achieve results’: Iran conveys terms to US for restarting talks
content: Iran has officially presented seven demands to Washington for resuming negotiations, emphasizing the need to conclude hostilities and unfreeze assets. Alongside this diplomatic approach, Iran is readying itself for potential US military actions, adapting its military strategy to prioritize naval capabilities. Efforts are underway to swiftly resolve the ongoing conflict.

title: Father-son duo makes history: Shigenobu and Koji light cauldron in Nagoya
content: Japan’s Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji Murofushi jointly lit the cauldron at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, bringing the torch relay to a memorable end. Both Shigenobu and Koji are former Asian Games champions in hammer throw. The duo climbed the stairs to the podium together before lighting the cauldron.

title: Atlanta man arrested after phone wipe; new ruling allows border searches
content: US border agents can now search traveler cellphones without reasonable suspicion or a warrant. A recent court ruling affirmed this broad authority at international borders. This decision follows an incident where a phone was wiped during an airport search. The ruling impacts traveler privacy and government access to electronic data. It highlights ongoing debates about digital device searches at the border.

title: Ken Griffey Jr.'s $2.5M Orlando estate now listed for $27m
content: Baseball legend Ken Griffey Jr. has placed his stunning lakeside mansion on the market for $27 million. Acquired in 2004, he dedicated four years to crafting this Mediterranean-style masterpiece, featuring seven luxurious bedrooms and ten bathrooms. The estate boasts exceptional amenities, including a private movie theater and a fun-filled saltwater pool complete with a waterslide. With his children now grown, Griffey is ready to pass on this remarkable home.

title: Alaska’s largest recorded gold nugget, found in 1998, later sold for $750,000
content: In Alaska, a miner's incredible find of a massive gold and quartz specimen led to the unveiling of the largest gold nugget ever discovered in the state. Weighing over twenty pounds, this extraordinary piece, known as the Alaska Centennial Nugget, was held in a private collection until it hit the auction block in 2021, where it fetched an impressive $750,000.

title: Johnny Carson’s Malibu estate once asked $81.5m, finally sold for $40m
content: Johnny Carson's iconic Malibu estate has embarked on quite a price adventure. Initially acquired for around nine point five million dollars, the property was later listed at eighty-one point five million dollars. It ultimately sold for forty million dollars in 2019 and has now returned to the market, boasting a staggering price tag of one hundred ten million dollars.

title: UPI MDR: Can Rs 6,000 be split into three Rs 2,000 payments? No daily cap
content: The NPCI framework and the FAQs issued with it do not stipulate that multiple payments relating to a single bill must be clubbed together. Such a restriction, if in place, could prevent businesses from breaking up larger payments into multiple transactions of Rs 2,000 or less.

title: Stephen Curry’s Oakland charity shares a milestone
content: Stephen Curry, the four time NBA champion, and his wife, Ayesha Curry's charity, Eat, Learn & Play has made an update on their achievemetns.

title: Why parents keep old report cards and childhood drawings, according to psychology
content: For parents, childhood drawings and school assignments go beyond mere artifacts of nostalgia; they encapsulate rich autobiographical memories and poignant family moments. Studies reveal that nostalgic feelings can elevate the perceived value of these everyday objects. Furthermore, these keepsakes serve as visual reminders of the swift journey through parenthood, capturing the essence of time spent in care and love.

title: She paid Rs 79l for Rs 2.14cr villa, but it stayed unfinished; RERA orders refund
content: The Telangana RERA authority noted that the builder had already collected Rs 79 lakh, but had not placed any material on record showing the current status of construction of the villa.

title: 'Nothing is wrong': Salman Khan's BB 20 promo sparks health concerns
content: Bigg Boss host Salman Khan took to social media to clarify recent concerns about his health following a dramatic promo release. He revealed that the chest pain depicted was merely a message directed at contestant Qazi and expressed his displeasure with how the promo was edited, emphasizing its misleading nature. Addressing online trolls, Khan boldly removed his hat and shirt to confront critics of his appearance.

title: 'My son was killed, tortured': Mother of IIT-Bombay student seeks justice after his death
content: An IIT Bombay student died by suicide in his hostel room after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during an exam, triggering protests on campus. The institute said no disciplinary action had been initiated and that the student had been counselled, while his mother alleged torture and demanded justice.

title: Psychology says feeling uneasy when someone is too kind doesn’t mean you’re ungrateful
content: Receiving kindness can be an uncomfortable experience for many, invoking feelings of awkwardness. This unease can originate from various psychological factors and past experiences. Some view kindness as an obligation or believe they must earn affection. Likewise, receiving compliments can conflict with one's self-perception. Cultivating the ability to accept little gestures of care can significantly reduce this discomfort.

title: Meet Neha Thakur, 25, Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver
content: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.

title: 'When she returns to movies': Salman Khan slams those trolling Katrina Kaif
content: Salman Khan took a stand against the harmful practice of body and age shaming that plagues the internet. In a show of vulnerability, he shed his shirt and makeup to confront his critics about their hurtful comments, especially towards those dealing with postpartum weight gain. Moreover, he expressed discontent over paparazzi taking inappropriate photos of female celebrities, voicing his disdain for online hate and personal invasions.

title: IIT-Bombay suicide: Parents refuse to take son's body; crime branch to probe case
content: The abetment of suicide case involving an IIT-Bombay student has been transferred to the crime branch.  An FIR was registered after the student's parents alleged casteist slurs and harassment.  The student was found dead in his hostel room on Friday.  His parents refused to claim the body until accused persons were arrested.  The investigation is ongoing, and IIT-Bombay will cooperate fully with authorities.

title: Yashasvi Solanki becomes first woman officer to serve as President’s ADC
content: Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki made history in May 2025 by becoming the first woman officer from India’s Army, Navy or Air Force to serve as Aide-de-Camp to the President. A Haryana native and former district-level badminton and volleyball player, Solanki joined the Indian Navy in 2012. Her journey from sports and naval service to Rashtrapati Bhavan highlights discipline, perseverance and the changing role of women in India’s armed forces.

title: 18 years after the 2008 financial meltdown: How a crisis born in US reshaped India
content: The 2008 global financial crisis hit India through markets, capital flows and trade, but its banking system remained resilient. The shock exposed gaps in financial resolution and regulation, prompting reforms including the IBC, stronger safeguards for systemically important banks and higher buffers. Nearly 18 years later, India is stronger, but rising AI investment raises fresh questions about leverage and financial stability.

title: England sweep Sri Lanka 3-0, replace India at top of T20I rankings
content: England beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the third T20I at Old Trafford in Manchester on Saturday to complete a 3-0 series sweep. The hosts chased down Sri Lanka's 125-run target with 62 balls to spare. The win also helped England move back to the top of the T20 world rankings, replacing India.

title: Invasive spotted lanternfly reaches Canada after spreading across 18 US states
content: Canada confirmed its first spotted lanternfly detection in Windsor, Ontario.  Movement restrictions are now in place to prevent further spread of this invasive species.  Surrounding areas are under surveillance to assess the infestation's extent.  This pest poses significant risks to agriculture and forestry industries.  Early detection and reporting are crucial for managing its impact.

title: Couple bought 5 acres for $27,000; three cabins later made over $2.1 million
content: Chris Broomfield transformed five acres into a thriving hospitality business. His first A-frame cabin generated significant revenue after its 2018 listing. Subsequent unique cabins, like a treehouse, also achieved substantial financial success. Broomfield's ventures have now earned over $2.1 million in total revenue. He continues to expand his cabin empire for his family's future.

The man also allegedly assaulted his wife when she intervened, days after she had moved back in with him following a court-directed attempt at reconciliation.

content: the seven time super bowl champion has always been public about fatherhood . the new England Patriots legend has reflected on fatherhood and the mistakes he has made . a few months ago, in his newsletter, Tom Brady opened up about dadhood as he wrote: "Remember, your children are watching everything. They see what you do in every aspect of your life and how you do it"

title: System threatened by students as they ask questions: Rahul
content:
The system wants ‘andh bhakts’, said Rahul

INDORE: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Saturday said the "system" created by top BJP politicians and certain businessmen controlling every aspect of governance in the country is threatened by students. Addressing youth at a 'Chhatron ki Goonj' in Indore, he said, "The system is threatened by students as they ask questions. That is why the system does not want students. The system wants 'andh bhakts'." He described students as embodiments of curiosity, love, humility, courage, tolerance and honesty, while characterising blind followers as "delusional, hateful, arrogant, cowardly, patriarchal and dishonest". Rahul also targeted NSA Ajit Doval, accusing him of enabling "surveillance of citizens' communication data to help govt exert control over the population".

End of Article

title: Ambulance stuck in mud, pregnant woman taken to hospital on bullock cart
content: pregnant woman was taken to hospital on a bullock cart and then a two-wheeler . she later delivered an intrauterine dead girl at the community health centre . villagers allege the poor road delayed treatment . doctors said the road condition had no bearing on the death .

title: Ellen DeGeneres’ restored Santa Barbara farmhouse relisted for $14.75 million
content: the 1917 farmhouse sits in the quiet Toro Canyon corridor, a scenic stretch of rural Santa Barbara County known for avocado groves, vineyards and wide-open views toward the Pacific . the four bedroom, five bathroom home on about 25 acres has now returned to the market with a relisting price of $14.75 million .

title: PM Modi pushes back on West’s narrative over emissions
content: PM Modi questioned the narrative in which the responsibility for carbon emissions is pinned on developing countries while Western countries are absolved of their role as historical polluters . he reaffirmed the country’s commitment to climate action and stressed that it has the best record among G20 countries .

title: SC 'banyan tree' of environmental justice: CJI Surya Kant

title: ASI Harjit Singh murdered: Key suspect shot dead in police encounter in Amritsar

title: As monsoon withdrawal begins, season may end with 10% deficit
